clue.text: Like one in the clue, they give a reader pause

definitions.text: Like one in the clue, they give a reader pause

parts.words: Like one in the clue, they give a reader pause
parts.note: the clue itself holds one of these punctuation marks, right after the word clue, and each one makes the reader halt briefly

explanation.surface: A remark about little marks that make someone reading slow down.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points at itself: the mark after 'clue' is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These punctuation marks signal a short break in a sentence, a pause for whoever reads it.

clue.text: Drink close to the parson's nose?

definitions.text: Drink close to the parson's nose?

parts.words: Drink close to the parson's nose?
parts.note: the parson's nose is the fleshy rump of a cooked fowl, which sits right by a bird's tail feathers; the whole is a mixed drink

explanation.surface: Someone sipping alcohol right under the vicar's nose.
explanation.walkthrough: The parson's nose is British slang for the tail end of a roast chicken; a cockerel's tail feathers lie close to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed alcoholic drink takes its name from a rooster's tail feathers.

clue.text: A fellow gets indisposed with a cheroot

parts.note: a fellow is a man
indisposed means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A man who smokes a cigar and feels sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar from the Philippine capital, a type of cheroot.

clue.text: Alcohol gives Ava quite a turn

indicators.note: a turn here is a twist, so the letters of the words given are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Drink makes a woman named Ava feel faint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a turn' looks like a fainting fit, but 'turn' signals an anagram of AVA QUITE A.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for water of life, an old term for strong spirits such as brandy.

clue.text: How a beastly crocodile escaped the flood

definitions.text: How a beastly crocodile escaped the flood

parts.words: How a beastly crocodile escaped the flood
parts.note: a crocodile is also a line of people walking in pairs; Noah's animals boarded the ark in pairs before the Flood

explanation.surface: A tale of how a reptile survived a deluge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crocodile' looks like the reptile, but it is the schoolchildren's line walking in pairs; 'beastly' makes it a line of animals going into Noah's ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals entered Noah's ark in pairs, one couple after another.

clue.text: Relish a Cowes rest-cure for a change

indicators.note: something changed is made different, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday at the Isle of Wight yachting town offers a break and a tasty treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes is a sailing resort on the Isle of Wight. 'for a change' suggests a holiday but is the anagram signal on A COWES REST-CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The spicy brown condiment is a sauce used to add savour to food.

clue.text: With transport at hand, get your hat!"

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport
by means near or close at hand

explanation.surface: Grab your hat, the bus is nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: A busby is the tall fur hat of some British soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A busby is a tall fur cap worn by hussars and some guardsmen.

clue.text: It's unimportant whether the test is about four or six

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the test wraps around the numeral

parts.note: a trial is a test
IV is Roman four and VI Roman six; either one fits inside to give the same letters

explanation.surface: Whether an exam lasts four or six hours makes no difference.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat touch: TR(IV)IAL and TRI(VI)AL both work, so it truly does not matter which.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial is of little consequence.

clue.text: As punctual as a Swiss cuckoo ?.

definitions.text: As punctual as a Swiss cuckoo ?.

parts.words: As punctual as a Swiss cuckoo ?.
parts.note: a Swiss cuckoo here is not a bird but a cuckoo clock, which pops out precisely at each hour

explanation.surface: Praise for an unusually reliable bird from Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: The cuckoo is the one in a cuckoo clock, the Swiss being famed for timepieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving punctually means arriving at the appointed hour, as a good clock keeps it.

clue.text: But a golfer as such doesn't need one

definitions.text: But a golfer as such doesn't need one

parts.words: But a golfer as such doesn't need one
parts.note: a golfer who drives hits off the tee, which needs no official permit, unlike one who drives a car

explanation.surface: A remark that golfers need no permit to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' in golf is hitting a long shot from the tee; the motorist's permit is not required for that.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists must hold this official permit to drive on public roads.

clue.text: He kept off the beaten track

definitions.text: He kept off the beaten track

parts.words: He kept off the beaten track
parts.note: read 'beaten track' not as a well-worn path but as the route of the defeated; this man never lost

explanation.surface: An explorer who avoided well-trodden paths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off the beaten track' suggests a remote route; read literally, he stayed out of the ranks of the beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor who subdues others is never among the defeated.

clue.text: Sartorial expedient

parts.note: the word means both a simple loose dress and a ... device or stratagem, so it is an expedient for the wardrobe

explanation.surface: A quick fix in matters of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose straight dress shares its name with a stopgap or dodge used to get by.

clue.text: Arrange a live TV location in the Middle East

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a new order, so the letters of the following words are reordered

explanation.surface: Organising an outside broadcast from somewhere in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' sounds like setting up a broadcast, but it is the anagram signal on A LIVE TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel's second city is a place in the Middle East.

clue.text: The last thing the Greeks wanted

definitions.text: The last thing the Greeks wanted

parts.words: The last thing the Greeks wanted
parts.note: not 'what they least desired' but what Greeks hoped for at the very end: the blessed afterlife of their myths

explanation.surface: Something the Greeks were dead against.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last thing they wanted' normally means something unwelcome; here it is what they wished for after death.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the heroic and virtuous dead went to this paradise as their final home.

clue.text: Not suitable for paint-mixing

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the letters of the word paint are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something unfit for stirring paint with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' is the anagram signal on PAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means inappropriate or ill-suited.

clue.text: There's not much in it for a cracksman!

definitions.text: There's not much in it for a cracksman!

parts.words: There's not much in it for a cracksman!
parts.note: a cracksman is a safebreaker, but here it is someone cracking nuts, who finds only a small kernel inside

explanation.surface: A safecracker complaining of a poor haul.
explanation.walkthrough: A cracksman is old slang for a burglar who cracks safes; the cracking here is of nuts, and the casing holds little.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard case of a nut encloses only a small kernel, hence the idiom for a brief summary.

clue.text: Carried by a Scots traveller talking nonsense?

definitions.text: Carried by a Scots traveller talking nonsense?

parts.words: Carried by a Scots traveller talking nonsense?
parts.note: havers is Scots for nonsensical talk, and a hiker carries a sack; together they suggest the hiker's bag

explanation.surface: A Scottish wanderer babbling as he goes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland, to haver is to talk nonsense, and a backpacker carries a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas bag carried on the back by walkers.

clue.text: Apparently not quick-growing plants

parts.note: climbing plants of this kind sound as though they move slowly, by inching along

explanation.surface: A gardener's note on slow-developing greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: The name of these plants sounds like slow movement, though many grow fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that trail or climb along the ground or walls, inching outwards.

clue.text: Social campaigner has a measure in the bar

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as the clue puts the measure within the bar

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise or lift
an ell is an old measure of length for cloth

explanation.surface: An activist who keeps a measure of drink at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is a crowbar. The Levellers were 17th-century English radicals seeking equality.
explanation.definitionFit: The Levellers were a radical group in the English Civil War who campaigned for social equality.

clue.text: Time for action by 18?

parts.note: the answer to 18 is someone who makes things level; what such a person does is the same word as a time of day

explanation.surface: Asking when the radical should move.
explanation.walkthrough: 18-across is a person who makes things equal; the act of making flat shares its spelling with the late part of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The latter part of the day, before night, is spelt like the act of making flat.

clue.text: A face-saving device

parts.note: face-saving usually means avoiding embarrassment; here a device that literally protects the face

explanation.surface: A trick for avoiding humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face-saving' suggests sparing someone's pride; here the face is protected physically, as by a helmet's front piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The movable front of a helmet shields the wearer's face.

clue.text: Dog might be the one that springs

definitions.text: Dog might be the one that springs

parts.words: Dog might be the one that springs
parts.note: springer is a breed name within this family of gun dogs, so the one that springs belongs to it

explanation.surface: A guess at which dog will leap.
explanation.walkthrough: The springer is a breed of gun dog, so the dog that 'springs' belongs to this family.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog family with long ears, including the English springer.

clue.text: _______ It devastated in Poland

parts.note: fill the blank with the city and split it into two words: a conflict that witnessed the place devastated

explanation.surface: A gap to fill about a ruined Polish place.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the missing word as two: armed conflict, then the past of see; that conflict witnessed the Polish capital ruined in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Poland's capital was largely destroyed during the Second World War.

clue.text: The French doctor, one appearing in account of old type of 26

indicators.note: the pieces show up within another, which places them inside the abbreviation

parts.note: le is French for the
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A French physician figures in a report on an antique piece of apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the answer at 26-across, a distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is the old flask-and-beak vessel alchemists used for distilling.

clue.text: She appears to be all upside down

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means the word all is read from the bottom up, backwards

explanation.surface: A woman who appears completely topsy-turvy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the reversed word is read bottom to top, which is why 'upside down' signals the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Bella is a woman's name, so a she.

clue.text: Measure of note in a beastly prison

indicators.note: the note is set inside the prison, as the clue's word for placement says

parts.note: a cage is a prison for animals
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Gauging the size of a note held in a zoo enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly prison' reads as a harsh jail, but it is an animal's enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is land area reckoned in acres, a measurement of extent.

clue.text: Yet the photograph might provide a moving spectacle

definitions.text: the photograph might provide a moving spectacle
definitions.meaning: a single frame taken from a film, so a photograph drawn from a moving picture

explanation.definitionFit: The word means nevertheless, and also a single publicity frame taken from a motion picture.

clue.text: Fruit one found in the entrance' perhaps

indicators.note: the single letter is discovered within the other piece, so it is placed inside
perhaps says the word entrance might be arranged otherwise, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit discovered in a doorway, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns ENTRANCE into NECTARNE, and 'found in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach.

clue.text: Probably he has some hair raising experiences

definitions.text: Probably he has some hair raising experiences

parts.words: Probably he has some hair raising experiences
parts.note: hair-raising usually means terrifying; here it means literally building up heads of hair

explanation.surface: A man whose job brings frightening moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair-raising' suggests terror; this craftsman raises hair in the sense of making false heads of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes wigs and perukes literally builds up false hair.

clue.text: What these bards suffered in hot water, say ?

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the words are spoken, not how they are written

parts.note: to scald is to burn with hot liquid, so they scalds

explanation.surface: Poets who got burnt in the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hot water' suggests trouble, but here it is literal: burning by hot liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Skalds were the poets of medieval Scandinavia, composing verse for kings.
